Abstract

This specification defines the first public Janus-QL Core query language contract implemented by the current validated Janus system for hybrid live-historical RDF querying.

1. Introduction

Janus-QL is a declarative query language for expressing windows over live RDF streams and historical RDF event logs, enabling correlation among both in a single query.

Janus-QL extends RSP-QL with window declarations over persisted RDF event logs. Projection, graph patterns, filters, aggregates, live windows, and the remaining query syntax are inherited from SPARQL and RSP-QL unless this specification states otherwise.

This specification defines the paper-aligned Janus-QL language core used for hybrid live-historical RDF querying. It focuses on the Janus-specific additions rather than reproducing the complete SPARQL or RSP-QL grammar.

Janus-QL supports three window forms in total:

  • live windows using ON STREAM [RANGE ... STEP ...];

  • fixed historical windows using ON LOG [START ... END ...]; and

  • sliding historical windows using ON LOG [OFFSET ... RANGE ... STEP ...].

1.1. Language Positioning

Janus-QL adopts the RSP-QL model in which named windows are declared over dynamic RDF sources and later referenced inside query graph patterns. Its distinguishing extension is the ability to declare named windows over a historical RDF event log using ON LOG.

This specification does not define Janus-QL as a complete SPARQL 1.1 or complete RSP-QL standard. Features that are not explicitly described here remain inherited only to the extent already defined by SPARQL or RSP-QL, and Janus-QL adds only the historical-window constructs described in this document.

2. Conformance

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY in this specification are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

A Janus-QL processor conforms to this specification if it accepts every query form defined by this specification and rejects every query form that this specification marks as unsupported or invalid.

This specification currently defines one conformance class: Janus-QL Core.

2.1. Janus-QL Core Conformance Class

A Janus-QL Core processor conforms to this specification if it:

  • supports the Janus-QL historical window declaration forms defined in this specification;

  • accepts live ON STREAM [RANGE ... STEP ...] windows as inherited from RSP-QL;

  • validates Janus-QL window declarations according to the rules in § 6 Window Declarations;

  • constructs the Streaming Dataset according to § 9 Streaming Dataset Construction and Query Evaluation; and

  • evaluates the resulting query algebra expression according to § 9 Streaming Dataset Construction and Query Evaluation and § 11 Window Evaluation Semantics.

Janus-QL Core consists of the following public language elements:

  • PREFIX declarations;

  • an optional REGISTER RStream <output> AS clause;

  • top-level SELECT queries;

  • FROM NAMED WINDOW declarations;

  • live ON STREAM [RANGE ... STEP ...] windows;

  • fixed historical ON LOG [START ... END] windows;

  • sliding historical ON LOG [OFFSET ... RANGE ... STEP ...] windows;

  • WINDOW <name> { ... } blocks;

  • basic graph patterns, filters, grouping, and aggregates inherited from SPARQL and RSP-QL; and

  • the Janus-QL RDF event, window, and Streaming Dataset semantics defined by this specification.

Historical-only nested subqueries, mixed nested-query rules, and other implementation-specific forms are not part of Janus-QL Core unless they are explicitly documented as non-normative implementation extensions.

3. Query Model

A Janus-QL query reuses the RSP-QL query shape of PREFIX declarations, an optional REGISTER RStream <output> AS clause, one top-level SELECT query, one or more FROM NAMED WINDOW declarations, and a WHERE clause containing WINDOW <name> { ... } graph-pattern blocks.

Janus-QL extends that model only by allowing a named window to be declared over a persisted historical RDF event log using ON LOG.

The public window declaration forms are:

  • FROM NAMED WINDOW <w> ON STREAM <s> [RANGE <r_l> STEP <delta_l>]

  • FROM NAMED WINDOW <w> ON LOG <l> [START <t_start> END <t_end>]

  • FROM NAMED WINDOW <w> ON LOG <l> [OFFSET <o> RANGE <r_h> STEP <delta_h>]

Janus-QL therefore supports three window forms in total:

  • live windows using ON STREAM [RANGE ... STEP ...];

  • fixed historical windows using ON LOG [START ... END ...]; and

  • sliding historical windows using ON LOG [OFFSET ... RANGE ... STEP ...].

Projection, graph patterns, filters, aggregates, live windows, and the remaining query syntax are inherited from SPARQL and RSP-QL. This specification does not reproduce the complete SPARQL or RSP-QL grammar.

4. Simplified Janus-QL Grammar

This section gives a simplified EBNF grammar for the Janus-QL core documented by this specification. Janus-QL extends the RSP-QL dataset clauses with fixed and sliding windows over historical RDF event logs while retaining the existing live-stream window form.

query ::=
    prefixDecl* REGISTER streamOp outputStream AS selectClause datasetClause+ whereClause

prefixDecl ::=
    PREFIX prefixName: iri

streamOp ::=
    RStream
    | IStream
    | DStream

selectClause ::=
    SELECT (
        *
        | projectionItem+
    )

projectionItem ::=
    variable
    | ( expression AS variable )

datasetClause ::=
    FROM NAMED WINDOW windowName windowSource

windowSource ::=
    ON STREAM streamName [ RANGE duration STEP duration ]
    | ON LOG logName [ START timeInstant END timeInstant ]
    | ON LOG logName [ OFFSET duration RANGE duration STEP duration ]

whereClause ::=
    WHERE { whereAtom+ }

whereAtom ::=
    graphPattern
    | WINDOW windowName { graphPattern }
    | { subquery }

subquery ::=
    SELECT (
        *
        | projectionItem+
    ) whereClause

In this grammar:

  • prefixName denotes a prefix name.

  • outputStream denotes the IRI of the registered output stream.

  • windowName denotes a window IRI.

  • streamName denotes a live RDF stream IRI.

  • logName denotes a historical RDF event log IRI.

  • variable denotes a SPARQL variable.

  • duration denotes a duration.

  • timeInstant denotes a time instant.

  • expression denotes a SPARQL expression.

  • graphPattern denotes a SPARQL graph pattern.

The grammar distinguishes the three window forms supported by Janus-QL:

  • a live window declared using ON STREAM ... [RANGE ... STEP ...];

  • a fixed historical window declared using ON LOG ... [START ... END ...]; and

  • a sliding historical window declared using ON LOG ... [OFFSET ... RANGE ... STEP ...].

5. Expression Fragment

Janus-QL Core defines a conservative SPARQL-style expression fragment for FILTER and HAVING.

This specification does not claim full SPARQL 1.1 expression conformance.

Janus-QL Core explicitly defines the following expression forms:

  • variable references;

  • RDF literals;

  • parenthesized expressions;

  • comparison expressions using =, !=, <, <=, >, and >=; and

  • aggregate result variables and grouping variables in HAVING.

FILTER expressions restrict the solution mappings produced by the surrounding graph-pattern evaluation.

HAVING expressions restrict grouped results after GROUP BY and aggregate evaluation.

The current validated Janus-QL Core examples and tests explicitly cover comparison-style FILTER expressions such as ?value > ?historicalAverage. This specification correspondingly defines a conservative HAVING fragment over grouping variables and aggregate result variables, without claiming broader SPARQL 1.1 expression support.

Janus-QL Core does not otherwise define full SPARQL 1.1 expression semantics. In particular, this specification does not define the following forms as part of Janus-QL Core unless a later version explicitly adds them:

  • EXISTS;

  • NOT EXISTS;

  • IN;

  • NOT IN;

  • regex;

  • function calls;

  • datatype casts;

  • arithmetic expressions;

  • bound();

  • isIRI();

  • isLiteral(); and

  • language-tag inspection or language-tag matching functions.

A Janus-QL processor MAY support additional SPARQL-like expression forms as implementation extensions. Such extensions are non-normative and do not expand Janus-QL Core.

6. Window Declarations

Janus-QL extends the RSP-QL dataset-clause syntax by allowing a named window to be declared over a persisted historical RDF event log using ON LOG.

6.1. Live Window

The following inherited RSP-QL form declares a live window over a live RDF stream:

FROM NAMED WINDOW <w> ON STREAM <s> [RANGE <r_l> STEP <delta_l>]

6.2. Fixed Historical Window

The following form declares a fixed historical window over a historical RDF event log:

FROM NAMED WINDOW <w> ON LOG <l> [START <t_start> END <t_end>]

A fixed historical window selects the events whose timestamps lie within the declared absolute interval.

6.3. Sliding Historical Window

The following form declares a sliding historical window over a historical RDF event log:

FROM NAMED WINDOW <w> ON LOG <l> [OFFSET <o> RANGE <r_h> STEP <delta_h>]

At evaluation instant T, the OFFSET identifies the distance between the current evaluation instant and the left boundary of the historical window. The historical window then covers the interval [T - o, T - o + r_h] and advances according to delta_h.

6.4. Validation Rules

The following Janus-QL validation rules are normative:

  • window identifiers MUST be unique;

  • ranges MUST be positive;

  • steps MUST be positive;

  • offsets MUST be non-negative;

  • a fixed historical window MUST satisfy t_start < t_end;

  • a sliding historical window MUST satisfy r_h <= o.

The condition r_h <= o is the Janus-QL past-only constraint. It ensures that the historical interval does not extend beyond evaluation instant T.

For a hybrid query that combines a sliding historical window with a live window of live range r_l, the query MUST also satisfy:

  • r_h + r_l <= o.

This is the Janus-QL no-overlap constraint. It ensures that the right boundary of the historical interval does not cross the left boundary of the live interval.

7. Window Blocks

A declared window is referenced inside WHERE by a WINDOW <name> { ... } block.

Example:

WINDOW ex:liveWindow {
  ?sensor ex:hasValue ?value .
}

A WINDOW <name> { ... } block MUST refer to a window name declared by a FROM NAMED WINDOW clause in the same query.

The graph pattern inside a WINDOW <name> { ... } block is evaluated against the materialized window graph selected by that declaration, as defined in § 8 RDF Event Model.

8. RDF Event Model

This section defines the RDF event model used by Janus-QL.

An RDF event is a pair e = (q, tau), where q is an RDF quad and tau is its associated timestamp.

A live RDF stream is a potentially unbounded sequence of RDF events,

S_live = <e_1, e_2, e_3, ...>,

in non-decreasing timestamp order, such that for every i >= 1, tau_i <= tau_(i+1).

A historical RDF event log is a finite ordered sequence of RDF events,

L = <e_1, e_2, ..., e_n>,

such that tau_i <= tau_(i+1).

At evaluation instant T, the visible historical RDF event log is:

L(T) = {(q, tau) in L | tau <= T}.

That is, L(T) contains exactly the historical RDF events whose timestamps are less than or equal to T.

8.1. Time-Varying Graphs

Each Janus-QL window declaration produces, at evaluation instant T, a time-varying graph selected from either a live RDF stream or a historical RDF event log.

For a declared window w, this specification writes the corresponding time-varying graph as G_w(T).

A pattern of the form:

WINDOW ex:w {
  P
}

is evaluated against the time-varying graph G_w(T) selected by that window declaration.

9. Streaming Dataset Construction and Query Evaluation

RSP-QL constructs named time-varying graphs from windows over live RDF streams.

Janus-QL extends that construction by allowing historical window operators over a historical RDF event log to produce named time-varying graphs with the same interface.

At evaluation instant T:

  • each live window produces a named time-varying graph;

  • each historical window produces a named time-varying graph; and

  • these graphs, together with the optional default graph and any static named graphs, form the unified Streaming Dataset SDS(T).

Janus-QL therefore modifies how the Streaming Dataset is populated, but it does not modify the underlying SPARQL algebra evaluation.

Once the live and historical windows have been converted into named time-varying graphs, the existing SPARQL and RSP-QL query-evaluation machinery is reused without modification:

eval(SDS(T), SE, T).

Here, SE is the query algebra expression.

Accordingly, Janus-QL extends the construction of the Streaming Dataset while preserving the subsequent RSP-QL evaluation semantics.

10. Implementation Extensions

This section is non-normative.

The language subset specified in this document does not require historical-only nested subqueries, mixed nested-query rules, or other optional query forms beyond the paper-aligned Janus-QL window model.

Implementations MAY support additional query forms for compatibility or experimentation. Such forms are implementation extensions and are outside Janus-QL Core unless a future version of this specification defines them normatively.

In particular, an implementation MAY continue to support historical-only nested subqueries for compatibility with existing systems. That behavior does not expand the Janus-QL Core semantics defined in this specification.

11. Window Evaluation Semantics

The semantics in this section operate over the RDF event model defined in § 8 RDF Event Model.

11.1. Fixed Historical Window Semantics

For a fixed historical window with bounds t_start and t_end, the time-varying graph at evaluation instant T is:

G_fixed(T) = { q | (q, tau) in L(T), t_start <= tau <= t_end } if T >= t_end, and G_fixed(T) = emptyset if T < t_end.

A fixed historical window becomes available only when its complete declared interval lies in the visible past.

Every fixed historical window MUST satisfy t_start < t_end.

11.2. Sliding Historical Window Semantics

For a sliding historical window at evaluation instant T with offset o, historical range r_h, and historical step delta_h, the time-varying graph is:

G_hist(T) = { q | (q, tau) in L(T), T - o <= tau <= T - o + r_h }.

The offset o identifies the distance between the current evaluation instant and the left boundary of the historical window.

The window advances according to delta_h.

Every sliding historical window MUST satisfy the past-only constraint r_h <= o.

For a hybrid query that combines a sliding historical window with a live window of live range r_l, the query MUST also satisfy the no-overlap constraint r_h + r_l <= o.

12. Examples

12.1. Hybrid Query Example

PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>

REGISTER RStream <output> AS
SELECT ((AVG(?liveCong) - AVG(?histCong)) AS ?delta)
FROM NAMED WINDOW ex:fixHist ON LOG <LOG_IRI> [START T_START END T_END]
FROM NAMED WINDOW ex:slidingHist ON LOG <LOG_IRI> [OFFSET O RANGE W STEP S]
FROM NAMED WINDOW ex:live ON STREAM <STREAM_IRI> [RANGE W_2 STEP S_2]
WHERE {
  WINDOW ex:fixHist {
    ?sensor ex:congestionLevel ?histCong .
  }
  WINDOW ex:slidingHist {
    ?sensor ex:congestionLevel ?histCong .
  }
  WINDOW ex:live {
    ?sensor ex:congestionLevel ?liveCong .
  }
}

This hybrid query contains one fixed historical window, one sliding historical window, and one live window. It combines values from the historical and live windows by comparing the average live congestion against the average historical congestion.

12.2. Additional Valid Examples

PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>

REGISTER RStream ex:output AS
SELECT ?sensor ?value
FROM NAMED WINDOW ex:liveWindow ON STREAM ex:stream [RANGE 60000 STEP 30000]
WHERE {
  WINDOW ex:liveWindow {
    ?sensor ex:hasValue ?value .
  }
}

This is a valid live-window query using the inherited RSP-QL ON STREAM [RANGE ... STEP ...] form.

PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>

SELECT ?sensor ?value
FROM NAMED WINDOW ex:historicalWindow ON LOG ex:archive [START 0 END 86400000]
WHERE {
  WINDOW ex:historicalWindow {
    ?sensor ex:hasValue ?value .
  }
}

This is a valid fixed historical-window query using ON LOG [START ... END ...].

12.3. Invalid Examples

PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>

SELECT ?sensor
FROM NAMED WINDOW ex:w ON LOG ex:archive [START 1000 END 1000]
WHERE {
  WINDOW ex:w {
    ?sensor ex:value ?value .
  }
}

A Janus-QL processor MUST reject this query because a fixed historical window must satisfy t_start < t_end.

PREFIX ex: <http://example.org/>

REGISTER RStream ex:output AS
SELECT ?sensor
FROM NAMED WINDOW ex:hist ON LOG ex:archive [OFFSET 1000 RANGE 2000 STEP 500]
FROM NAMED WINDOW ex:live ON STREAM ex:stream [RANGE 1000 STEP 500]
WHERE {
  WINDOW ex:hist {
    ?sensor ex:value ?histValue .
  }
  WINDOW ex:live {
    ?sensor ex:value ?liveValue .
  }
}

A Janus-QL processor MUST reject this query because it violates the past-only constraint r_h <= o and therefore also fails the hybrid no-overlap validation model.

13. Limitations

DEFINE BASELINE and USING BASELINE are not part of the public Janus-QL specification.

Historical-only nested subqueries, mixed nested-query rules, and other compatibility features are not part of Janus-QL Core. If an implementation supports them, that behavior is a non-normative implementation extension.

This specification does not define additional Janus-QL syntax beyond:

  • live windows using ON STREAM [RANGE ... STEP ...];

  • fixed historical windows using ON LOG [START ... END ...]; and

  • sliding historical windows using ON LOG [OFFSET ... RANGE ... STEP ...].

SPARQL and RSP-QL features beyond the query forms and semantics described in this specification are outside Janus-QL Core. This includes unsupported result-stream operators, arbitrary nested subqueries, SERVICE, property paths, and other extensions not defined in this document.
